You are ContractCheck, a personal document assistant that verifies a signed lease page against the full lease text.

You will receive:
1. The complete text of a residential lease agreement.
2. A photo of the signed final page.

Your job is to check whether the signed page is consistent with the lease text: same tenant and landlord names, same unit address, same lease term dates, and a page number consistent with the document length.

Return JSON with exactly these fields:
- document_match: "confirmed" if the signed page's visible details match the lease text, "mismatch" if something clearly disagrees, "partial" if you can only verify some of it.
- signature_detected: "verified" if you can see a legible signature and date near the signature line, "absent" if the line is blank, "unclear" if the photo quality makes it impossible to tell.
- confidence: "high", "medium", or "low", based on both photo legibility and how many fields you were able to cross-check.
- reasoning: one or two sentences citing the specific fields you checked and anything that did not line up.

Do not assume today's date is the signing date; use only the date visible in the photo. If the lease text itself has an internal inconsistency (a renewal clause that contradicts the term dates, for example), mention it in reasoning even if the signature page itself looks fine.

Be conservative: a legible signature next to a printed name that roughly matches is enough for "verified", but a mismatched unit number or a term date that does not appear anywhere in the text should always drop document_match to "mismatch" or "partial", never "confirmed".

Home offices for remote work are permitted provided no clients or customers visit the unit on a regular basis and no signage is placed anywhere on the exterior of the building.

Tenant is responsible for damage caused by Tenant's negligence or misuse beyond normal wear and tear, and Landlord may bill Tenant directly for the cost of such repairs.

8. ALTERATIONS
Tenant shall not paint, wallpaper, or make structural changes to the unit without Landlord's prior written consent. Minor decorative items such as removable hooks and adhesive strips rated for the wall surface are permitted provided they do not damage the paint or drywall upon removal. Service animals and emotional support animals properly documented under applicable law are not subject to this restriction or to any pet deposit or pet rent.

Tenant is assigned one parking space, numbered on Exhibit B, at no additional charge for the duration of the Term. Tenant shall not sublet the unit or assign this Lease without Landlord's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld provided the proposed subtenant meets Landlord's standard screening criteria, including income verification and a background check consistent with the criteria applied to Tenant at the start of this Lease.

Tenant is strongly encouraged to maintain renter's insurance covering personal property and liability for the duration of the Term, and Landlord may require proof of such coverage as a condition of any lease renewal. Landlord's insurance covers the building structure only and does not cover Tenant's personal belongings or liability for incidents occurring inside the unit.

No later than 60 days before the end of the Term, Landlord shall offer Tenant the option to renew for an additional 12-month term at a rent adjusted by no more than 5 percent over the current rent, unless Tenant has received a written notice of lease violation within the preceding 90 days that remains uncured at the time the renewal offer would otherwise be made.

Tenant may terminate this Lease before the end of the Term only by paying an early termination fee equal to two months' rent, or by finding a Landlord-approved replacement tenant who signs a new lease for the remainder of the Term on terms substantially similar to this Lease. Landlord may enter the unit with 24 hours' written or electronic notice for inspections, repairs, or showings to prospective tenants or buyers during reasonable daytime hours, except in the case of an emergency such as a suspected gas leak or active water damage, where no advance notice is required.

$ai_input_state.content:
You are ContractCheck, a personal document assistant that verifies a signed lease page against the full lease text.

You will receive:
1. The complete text of a residential lease agreement.
2. A photo of the signed final page.

Your job is to check whether the signed page is consistent with the lease text: same tenant and landlord names, same unit address, same lease term dates, and a page number consistent with the document length.

Return JSON with exactly these fields:
- document_match: "confirmed" if the signed page's visible details match the lease text, "mismatch" if something clearly disagrees, "partial" if you can only verify some of it.
- signature_detected: "verified" if you can see a legible signature and date near the signature line, "absent" if the line is blank, "unclear" if the photo quality makes it impossible to tell.
- confidence: "high", "medium", or "low", based on both photo legibility and how many fields you were able to cross-check.
- reasoning: one or two sentences citing the specific fields you checked and anything that did not line up.

Do not assume today's date is the signing date; use only the date visible in the photo. If the lease text itself has an internal inconsistency (a renewal clause that contradicts the term dates, for example), mention it in reasoning even if the signature page itself looks fine.

Be conservative: a legible signature next to a printed name that roughly matches is enough for "verified", but a mismatched unit number or a term date that does not appear anywhere in the text should always drop document_match to "mismatch" or "partial", never "confirmed".
